prism-2014-junior-01.prompt: By how much is 50% of 50 greater than 50% of 40?

prism-2014-junior-02.prompt: Which of the following numbers is the largest?

prism-2014-junior-03.prompt: How many whole numbers between 1 and 40 are either a multiple of 7 or end in a 7?

prism-2014-junior-04.prompt: The sun will rise in Galway tomorrow at 08:04 and set at 18:38. At what time will true midday be in Galway tomorrow if true midday is exactly halfway between these two times?

prism-2014-junior-05.prompt: If one loaf of bread can be traded for 4 eggs, and one chocolate bar can be traded for 2 eggs, how many chocolate bars are worth 3 loaves of bread?

prism-2014-junior-06.prompt: Three boys ate a total of 18 sweets. If Peter ate more sweets than each of the other two boys, what is the smallest number of sweets that Peter could have eaten?

prism-2014-junior-07.prompt: In how many ways can the four people A, B, C and D be seated in four chairs in a row?

prism-2014-junior-08.prompt: In a football tournament involving 10 teams, each team plays exactly three games. How many games will be played?

prism-2014-junior-09.prompt: If we write the number $\frac1{62500}$ as a decimal with the smallest possible number of digits, how many digits will appear after the decimal point?

prism-2014-junior-10.prompt: If we arrange the digits of the number 123 in all possible ways, we end up with a total of 6 three-digit numbers 123, 132, etc. What is the sum of these 6 three-digit numbers?

prism-2014-junior-11.prompt: How many simultaneous solutions do the equations $4x + 3y = 4$ and $4x + 2y = 4$ have?

prism-2014-junior-12.prompt: Twelve sweaters and eight shirts cost twenty euros more than eight sweaters and twelve shirts. We can say that

choices.text: a sweater costs the same as a shirt
a sweater costs €2.50 more than a shirt
a sweater costs €4 more than a shirt
a sweater costs €5 more than a shirt
a sweater costs €1 less than a shirt

prism-2014-junior-13.prompt: Of the 70 students who wrote an exam, 40 were male, 50 were from Galway and 20 were males who were from Galway. How many of the 70 students were neither male nor from Galway?

prism-2014-junior-14.prompt: A car went up a hill at 30 km/h and went down the same hill at a speed of 45 km/h. What was the average speed of the car in km/h for the entire journey?

prism-2014-junior-15.prompt: A chessboard has 64 squares. Suppose that one cent is placed on the first square, 2 cents on the second square, 3 cents on the third square, and so on up to 64 cents on the 64th square. What is the total amount of money (in cents) that will be placed on the board?

prism-2014-junior-16.prompt: In a 1000m race, Andrew beat Brian by 200m and Brian beat Charlie by 200m. By how many metres did Andrew beat Charlie? Assume that each person runs at a constant speed.

prism-2014-junior-17.prompt: Suppose that $a$, $b$ and $c$ are positive whole numbers that satisfy $ab = 6$, $ac = 18$ and $bc = 27$. What is the value of $abc$?

prism-2014-junior-18.prompt: Which of the following has the greatest perimeter?

choices.text: A square with sides of length 5 cm
A square with diagonal length equal to $\sqrt{50}$ cm
A square with area equal to 25 cm$^2$

prism-2014-junior-19.prompt: When we square the length of the diagonal of a square, the number of cm$^2$ that results is equal to four times the perimeter of the square in centimetres. What is the area of the square (in cm$^2$)?

prism-2014-junior-20.prompt: A class of $n$ students wrote an exam. After the exams were marked, $m$ of the students had their marks raised by 3 each and the remaining students had their marks raised by 1 each. The new average mark of the class is 1.5 more than the original average before the raises. What proportion, $\frac mn$, of the class had their marks raised by 3?
